systemic: Mixed pixel density: Minecraft textures scaled to arbitrary sizes (4-12 screen px per texel) beside smooth vector shapes; some sprites are bilinear-blurred. This is the largest single reason no chapter exceeds 7.
Sticker halo: per-sprite outline glows make props look cut out and pasted; there is no scene-wide light source or cast light.
Hotbar rows: evenly spaced item sprites on a rail across the bottom in ~10 chapters read as an inventory UI, not a scene.
Flat unshaded vector props (anvils, towers, pumpjack, mine entrance, livestock) next to textured pixel props.
Raw block faces (stone, ore, casings, bricks) blown up as scenery look like Minecraft blocks glued on, not illustration.
Composition: panels cluster centre-top, bottom-left/right often empty; hero props cropped by frame edges; objects float without ground contact.
Reused clip-art motifs across chapters (ray sun, pill-window tower, lantern) and debug-looking accents (red rings, dotted lines, sparkle clusters).
Contradictory atmospherics (sun + aurora + lightning; moon in an infirmary) break mood.
ceiling_estimate: About 7.5 for most chapters, maybe 8 for the best ones (stone_age, create, space, food) after fixes. Spec work (move things inward, remove hotbar rows, ground objects, cut contradictory elements) gets most chapters from 5.5-6.5 to 7. Renderer work (snap all sprites to one integer texel size, no smooth scaling, a scene-wide light pass with cast light and rim light instead of halos, shaded vector props, depth haze per layer) could reach 7.5-8. 9 is not realistic: it needs one coherent rendering style with bespoke, hand-authored compositions, real lighting and depth, and every element drawn for its place. Fraction-placed procedural motifs plus re-scaled game icons cannot get there, because the parts were never designed to sit together. To reach 9 you would need a different medium: hand-painted or hand-pixelled chapter illustrations (commissioned, or AI-generated and then hand-cleaned to one palette and density), imported as the scene layer.
